session_cue.text: Sir Phidipaldi slapping the Reeve with his glove

previous.text: The party reached Brandonsford at sunset, following a treasure map to places they did not recognize.
Reginald the frog warned the party to avoid a Clurichen trickster that comes into town every night.
Eric the Reeve offered a bounty on a black dragon that took a woodsman's arm. Sir Phidipaldi then slapped Eric with his glove.
Lady Hilda offered to hire on with the party, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would return after seeing the Reeve.
Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for hire, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.
Bentley and Farmer Gill told the party that supplies have stopped reaching Brandonsford.
Quinn promised Sir Phidipaldi payment for helping him get back at rival tavern keeper Bentley.

current.where_you_are: Sir Phidipaldi is at the bar of the empty Golden Egg Tavern with its owner, Quinn. Wayman Tisdale and Dr. Uriah are across the street in the Clumsy Fox Tavern, where Bentley has let them stay. Dunk is at Farmer Gill's farm, drinking with a very drunk Gill on the porch before bedding down in the barn.

Your goals.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley and collect his promised 100 gold.
Find the treasure on the party's treasure map.
Kill the black dragon outside Brandonsford and drag its body into town for Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Buy Farmer Gill's mule Shamus for 100 gold.

What could help.text: If Sir Phidipaldi and Quinn stage a showy fake ale delivery at the Golden Egg, they could see who comes for the stock.
If the party pays Lady Hilda, she will join them against the dragon.
The party has a treasure map marking several unfamiliar locations around Brandonsford.
If Dunk kills the dragon outside town, Farmer Gill might trade him Shamus. Gill never actually agreed to this.

Still unanswered.text: Who or what empties Quinn's stock every night?
What does the Clurichen do in Brandonsford each night?
What is stopping goods from reaching Brandonsford?
Where has this new dragon come from?

Meanwhile.text: The black dragon has already taken the woodsman George's arm, and Farmer Gill's three sons are hunting it now.

threads.name: The treasure map
threads.note: The party is following a treasure map whose marked locations they do not recognize; the treasure is still unfound.

threads.name: The Clurichen trickster
threads.note: Reginald warned that a trickster called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night up to no good, an open danger and question.

threads.name: The dragon and Eric the Reeve's bounty
threads.note: Eric offered 1000 gold for killing the black dragon and dragging its body into town (beat_18), and the rumours, George's encounter, Gill's sighting and his sons' hunt all bear on this one dragon. Sir Phidipaldi's insult and duel challenge to Eric (beat_20, beat_21) strained relations with the bounty-giver but did not end the offer.

threads.name: Lady Hilda's offer to join the party
threads.note: Lady Hilda said she cannot kill the dragon herself but would join adventurers for money, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would talk to the Reeve and come back for her services; her stated purpose ties her to the dragon hunt.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer of hire
threads.note: The thief Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for 100 gold a week, with a per-kill rebate, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

threads.name: Brandonsford's missing shipment
threads.note: The town's restocking shipment is a week overdue and goods have not reached town in months; nobody has yet gone after it.

threads.name: Farmer Gill's mule Shamus
threads.note: Gill offered Dunk the mule for 100 gold; Dunk asked to trade work, Gill pointed to killing the dragon, and Dunk is sleeping on the offer with no deal settled.

threads.name: Warwick's mithril chain shirt
threads.note: Warwick the increasingly paranoid smith displays a superb mithril chain shirt he refuses to sell, an item the party may want.

threads.name: Quinn's deal against Bentley
threads.note: Quinn's stock vanishes nightly and he blames Bentley; Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help get back at Bentley for 100 gold and to stage a fake ale delivery. The mystery of the vanishing stock bears directly on this deal, so it is one situation.

facts.text: Find the treasure the party's treasure map leads to.
The party holds a treasure map marking several locations around Brandonsford that they do not recognize.

classification.support_basis: The map is the party's only guide to where the treasure might be, though they cannot yet match its marked locations to real places.

facts.text: Where is the treasure the party's map marks?

classification.grounding_justification: Play states the party does not recognize the map's marked locations and only assumes the treasure lies at one of them.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying the marked places would largely settle it; no hidden circumstance is suggested.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: The answer is mainly instrumental to finding the treasure.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Matching the map to unknown land could involve asking locals and exploring the surrounding area.

facts.text: Reginald the frog warns that a little trickster called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Reginald only says it is up to no good and to stay away; no specific harm is named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Described as a little trickster; nothing suggests more than mischief or minor harm.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on the testimony of a single talking frog, a local witness of uncertain reliability.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald says it comes into town every night, an ongoing pattern, though no escalation is shown.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can avoid where it goes as advised, or watch for it at night, though means of stopping it are unclear.

facts.text: What does the Clurichen do when it comes into Brandonsford each night?

classification.grounding_justification: Reginald's warning that it is up to no good every night clearly raises what it is doing without saying.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden nightly activity and the creature's intentions.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning the trickster's nightly doings could explain mischief in town, but nothing yet makes it a major revelation.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It could be pursued by watching the riverbanks at night, following the creature, or questioning townsfolk.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon outside Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
Lady Hilda offers to join the party's dragon hunt for pay.

classification.support_basis: A seasoned, armoured fighter would strengthen the party against the dragon, though she says she cannot kill it alone.
classification.action_basis: Hilda explicitly offered to join adventurers hunting the dragon in exchange for money.

facts.text: George, a capable woodsman who lost an arm to the dragon and describes it as a black dragon, not a big one, lives a couple of houses from the Clumsy Fox and might come to the tavern tonight; the party could ask him where and how he met it.

classification.support_basis: George is the one known eyewitness who fought the dragon and could help the party find and prepare for it.
classification.action_basis: Eric only mentioned George and that he might show up; nobody offered his help.

facts.text: Where is the black dragon's lair?

classification.grounding_justification: Several people have seen the dragon outside town, but nobody has said where it lives; the gap arises mainly because the detail was not given.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single discovery of its location would settle it.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Witnesses George and Gill's sons could plausibly be questioned or tracked to find it.

facts.text: Where has this dragon come from, when nothing like it has been seen since Sir Brandon's dragon was killed centuries ago?

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley and Gill both stress that no dragon has appeared since Sir Brandon's was definitely killed, and Gill says he doesn't know where dragons come from, making the return conspicuous.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden cause behind the dragon's appearance after centuries.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: It could tie the current dragon to the town's founding legend of Sir Brandon and the fairy's sword.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The legend, local lore and the dragon itself offer leads to follow.

facts.text: The black dragon outside Brandonsford has already taken the woodsman George's arm, and Farmer Gill's three sons are out hunting it now.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Maiming or death of those who confront it, as George's lost arm shows, is a specific identifiable harm.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: The dragon has already maimed a capable woodsman, and Gill's sons risk serious injury or death.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George's injury is reported by Eric and Gill saw the dragon himself, but the dragon avoided Gill and nothing shows it attacking the town.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Gill's sons are actively hunting it now, setting up a confrontation, though no outcome is reported.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could kill the dragon or find Gill's sons first, but where they are is unknown.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned-looking noblewoman with chain mail and a shield, offers to join the party for pay to go after the dragon; no fee has been set.

classification.support_basis: She would add an armored, more experienced fighter to a party facing a dragon that took a capable woodsman's arm, though she says she cannot kill it alone.
classification.action_basis: Lady Hilda explicitly offered to join adventurers for money, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would come back for her services.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk with Eric the Reeve and then come back to take up her services.

classification.stake_basis: Hilda only offered her services for money; nothing shows she relies on the party returning beyond a possible paid job.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned offers himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, as long as he gets to kill people with the wasp; for a night of guaranteed kills he would rebate 5 gold per kill if he can do what he wants with the bodies.

classification.support_basis: Ned would add a killer and a fast-killing wasp to the party, but play tied his hire to no specific want or debt.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered his services and terms, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it, but no want or debt the hire would advance was named.

facts.text: What is stopping goods from reaching Brandonsford? Bentley says his restocking shipment is a week overdue, and Gill says nothing has come into town in months.

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley explicitly says the shipment never arrived and hurts the whole town, Wayman asked whether anyone had gone after it, and Gill independently says nothing has reached town in months.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the hidden cause behind months of missing goods, an underlying circumstance rather than a simple fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Explaining a months-long supply cutoff would change the party's understanding of the town's troubles, possibly linking to other local problems, though no link is established.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Finding the cause naturally invites following the supply route and questioning townsfolk.

facts.text: Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus, which Gill offers for 100 gold.
When Dunk asked to trade work for Shamus, Farmer Gill pointed to killing the dragon outside town as the big work needed; no deal is settled.
facts.uncertain_reason: Gill only named the dragon as the work needed; he never explicitly agreed to give Shamus for it.

classification.support_basis: Killing the dragon could let Dunk get Shamus without paying 100 gold, though it is unclear Gill would actually accept it as payment.
classification.action_basis: Gill answered Dunk's request to trade work by naming dragon-slaying as the work needed, but no terms were agreed.

facts.text: Why is Warwick the smith growing more paranoid, adding lucky charms to his shop every day? Gill guesses it is to keep away Ingrid the potion seller, who he says is hot for Warwick.

classification.grounding_justification: Gill explicitly describes Warwick's growing paranoia and daily charms, including a wall of clovers, as an oddity and offers only a speculative explanation.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal Warwick's hidden motive or fear, an underlying intention or circumstance.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting local color; it could explain his behavior but is not tied to larger events by the evidence.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: The party could question Warwick, Ingrid or townsfolk, plausibly following a few leads.

facts.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley and collect Quinn's promised 100 gold.

Quinn and Sir Phidipaldi plan to stage a fake ale delivery at the Golden Egg: Quinn brings bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering them, to see who comes for the stock.

classification.support_basis: The bait delivery could expose whoever empties Quinn's bar at night, which the party needs before acting against Bentley; it is untested whether the culprit will take the bait.
classification.action_basis: Quinn proposed and Sir Phidipaldi agreed to a specific staged delivery meant to reveal what happens to the stock.

facts.text: Who or what empties and knocks over Quinn's stock every night? Quinn blames Bentley.

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn explicitly describes a recurring nightly anomaly of a full bar found half-emptied or knocked over, and offers only an unproven suspicion.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer reveals a hidden nightly culprit and their method, possibly contradicting Quinn's assumption about Bentley.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Identifying the culprit would explain the Golden Egg's troubles and could confirm or overturn Quinn's grudge against Bentley.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: A staged bait delivery is already planned, and watching the bar or questioning Bentley offer further leads.
